sources.entry: Static Web Server - Cross-platform, high-performance, and asynchronous web server for static file serving. (Source Code) Apache-2.0/MIT Rust/Docker

summary.one_liner: A cross-platform, high-performance asynchronous web server written in Rust for serving static files.
summary.what_it_does: Static Web Server (SWS) serves static files over HTTP/1, HTTP/2 and TLS, built on Hyper and Tokio. It supports on-the-fly compression (Gzip, Deflate, Brotli, Zstandard) and serving pre-compressed .br, .gz and .zst files from disk. It also offers byte-range serving, Cache-Control and ETag defaults, optional directory listing (HTML or JSON, with .tar.gz download), CORS, and Basic HTTP auth with BCrypt. Routing features include URL rewrites and redirects, virtual hosting with per-host roots, SPA fallback pages, and custom error pages. Operations features include a health check endpoint, a Prometheus metrics endpoint, maintenance mode, structured JSON and file logging, graceful shutdown, and configuration via CLI, environment variables, or TOML. The README says it is available for Linux, macOS, Windows, FreeBSD, NetBSD, Android and Docker. The README describes v3 as in development and recommends v2 (LTS) for production use.
use_cases: serve a static website or single-page app
host static files behind a reverse proxy
serve static assets with compression and caching
run a small file server in Docker
expose Prometheus metrics for a static web server
serve files with HTTP basic auth
how_to_run: Refer to the project documentation website for installation and usage details
Download a pre-compiled release binary or pull a Docker image (Scratch, Alpine, or Debian variants)
Configure via CLI arguments, environment variables, or a TOML file
notable: Single ~4 MB static binary with zero runtime dependencies (Musl libc)
Serves pre-compressed .br, .gz and .zst files directly and compresses on the fly
Markdown content negotiation serves .md files to clients accepting text/markdown
Socket activation (systemd) and Windows Service support
Available as a Rust library with opt-in features
caveats: The README says v3 is in development; v2 (LTS) is recommended for production use
Installation and detailed usage are only in the external documentation website, not the README
